takeaways: A February 2026 driving tour of Saint Paul. Mississippi River Boulevard runs along the river with homes from about $500,000 to $2 million, many of them remodeled or rebuilt, and Hidden Falls Regional Park nearby.

Highland Bridge, on the former Ford plant site, is a multi-year redevelopment with new single-family homes from about $800,000, townhomes, shops and river trails. Ford Parkway around Cleveland and Finn is one of the city's most walkable stretches.

Macalester-Groveland, near Macalester College and the University of St. Thomas, has homes built mostly from about 1920 to 1970, priced from the mid-$300,000s to mid-$800,000s, plus Grand Avenue shops and the historic Grandview Theater.

Summit Avenue keeps about 85% of its original historic homes, including the Governor's Residence and the James J. Hill House. Jason's team sold a Summit Hill home for $2.3 million, the highest public sale in the area in about five years. Victorian homes need careful inspection.

Downtown and West Seventh: the Cathedral of Saint Paul, the Minnesota History Center, Grand Casino Arena (home of the Wild), Mancini's, Cossetta's, the Science Museum, Harriet Island, Union Depot, the farmers market and CHS Field (home of the Saints, the Twins' Triple-A team).
Around Como Lake, homes run from the upper $200,000s to about $500,000, close to the free Como Zoo and Conservatory, one of the oldest zoos in the country.
Overall, Saint Paul's median sits in the low to mid-$300,000s, more affordable than Minneapolis. Jason's advice: spend a weekend in each city before you choose.

faq.q: What is being built on the old Ford plant site in Saint Paul?
faq.a: Highland Bridge: a large mixed-use neighborhood with single-family homes (from about $800,000 in the video), townhomes, condos, shops and river trails, built out over several years.
Yes. Como Park Zoo and Conservatory in Saint Paul is free and supported by donations. It opened in the 1890s, making it one of the oldest zoos in the country.

faq.q: What was Saint Paul's original name?
faq.a: Pig's Eye, after fur trader Pierre "Pig's Eye" Parrant. The name changed after a Catholic priest named the settlement's chapel for Saint Paul.

takeaways: A 2025 tour of a new five-bedroom, five-bath walkout home of about 4,000 square feet in a new Inver Grove Heights neighborhood, with quick access to Highway 52 and I-494.

The main level has 9-foot ceilings, light-stained oak cabinets taller than the usual 42-inch uppers, a five-burner cooktop with a custom hood, a pantry with pull-outs, an office and a mudroom built-in. Andersen windows and hard siding throughout.
Upstairs are a loft and four bedrooms with walk-in closets, including the owner's suite (connected to the laundry room through the closet) and a second suite with its own bath.
The finished walkout lower level adds a fireplace, a bar and game area, a fifth bedroom with a walk-in closet, a three-quarter bath and storage. The stairs are at least 48 inches wide.

faq.q: Is there new construction in Inver Grove Heights?
faq.a: Yes. This 2025 tour shows a new five-bedroom walkout home close to Highway 52 and I-494.

takeaways: A 2025 tour of a Lennar villa model in the Royal Oak community in Lake Elmo, backing up to trees and a golf course.

One-level living on the main floor: an open kitchen with a large island, living and dining rooms with a deck, the owner's suite with a tiled shower and private water closet, a second bedroom or flex room and a full bath. The model has 10-foot ceilings and a three-car garage.
The large lookout lower level adds living space, another bath and a big storage room that could become an exercise room. Priced under $800,000 at the time.

faq.q: Are there one-level homes in Lake Elmo?
faq.a: Yes. Lennar's villa homes at Royal Oak in Lake Elmo put the owner's suite, laundry and living areas on the main floor, with a lower level for guests and storage.

takeaways: A 2025 tour of a Cuddigan custom home in The Wilds golf community in Prior Lake, priced at $1,175,000 at the time.
Prior Lake is close to Highway 169, about 8 miles from I-35, and within reach of MSP Airport. The lake itself is two connected bodies of water, about 1,600 acres in all by Jason's estimate.

The main level offers one-level living: 10-foot ceilings, oak floors and ceiling beams, a four-season porch, an eat-in kitchen with a six-burner range and Fisher & Paykel appliances, a large walk-through pantry, a mudroom and laundry, and an owner's suite with heated bathroom floors.
The lower level has a landing with a patio door, a family room with a fireplace, a wet bar, three bedrooms, a bath with twin sinks and plenty of storage, on its own heating zone.
Outside: a maintenance-free deck and siding, irrigation and finished landscaping. Four bedrooms, three baths and a finished three-car garage in all.

faq.q: What is The Wilds in Prior Lake?
faq.a: A golf course community in Prior Lake that's been around for nearly three decades, with custom homes from builders like Cuddigan.

takeaways: The North Loop shows what can happen to an old industrial area: a warehouse district for most of the 1900s, then artists, developers, restaurants and condos. Today it's one of the most in-demand parts of Minneapolis, with condos from the high $300,000s.
Upper Harbor Terminal, 48 acres of city-owned riverfront in North Minneapolis's McKinley neighborhood, was a barge terminal from 1968 until 2014 and sat empty for over a decade.

Ground broke in May on a roughly $350 million project. Its centerpiece is an 8,000-seat outdoor amphitheater run by First Avenue and the Minnesota Orchestra, with about 50 ticketed events a year, opening summer 2027.

Also planned: a 20-acre riverfront park running about a mile along the Mississippi with separate bike and walking trails (summer 2026), about 520 housing units, about 45,000 square feet of commercial space, a health and wellness hub and about 300 living-wage jobs.
Ground-lease revenue from private development goes into a 99-year community fund. Jason sees it as a long-term story for North Minneapolis, though no one can promise how it plays out.

faq.q: What is the Upper Harbor Terminal project?
faq.a: A roughly $350 million redevelopment of 48 acres of Mississippi riverfront in North Minneapolis, with an 8,000-seat amphitheater, a 20-acre riverfront park, about 520 homes and new commercial space.

faq.q: When does the Upper Harbor amphitheater open?
faq.a: The amphitheater, run by First Avenue and the Minnesota Orchestra, is expected to open in summer 2027, according to the video. The riverfront park is expected in summer 2026.

takeaways: Jason's five favorite places to move in 2026, with prices as stated in the video. Eagan, around Lebanon Hills Regional Park (nearly 2,000 acres, the largest park in Dakota County): median about $417,000, homes selling in about 28 days, 15 minutes to the Mall of America and 20 to 30 minutes to either downtown.

Credit River: incorporated as a city in 2021, with custom homes on 2.5 to 10 acres and a median listing price around $1.3 million. Newer developments include The Ranch and Yellowstone, and The Legends Golf Club is in town.

Elko New Market: median sale price about $385,000, about 30 minutes to downtown Minneapolis via I-35. There's no grocery store in town yet, but you get a quieter, small-town pace, plus Elko Speedway (racing since the 1960s) and one of the few remaining outdoor movie screens.

Northfield: median sale price about $363,000 (up 8.4%), a historic downtown on the Cannon River, Carleton and St. Olaf colleges, the Defeat of Jesse James Days festival, the Cowling Arboretum and its own hospital.
Waconia: median sale price about $435,000, on Lake Waconia, near Carver Park Reserve, with Waconia Brewing, Schram Vineyards and Lola's Lake House.
Bonus: St. Bonifacius, 4 to 6 miles from Waconia, with a median around $345,000 and a famously popular local meat market and deli.

faq.q: How big is Lebanon Hills Regional Park?
faq.a: Nearly 2,000 acres in Eagan and Apple Valley, the largest park in Dakota County, with trails for hiking, mountain biking and cross-country skiing.

faq.q: Does Elko New Market have a grocery store?
faq.a: Not yet, according to the video. Residents drive about 10 to 12 miles to nearby stores in Lakeville and surrounding towns.
